question: What is the smallest durable and scalable Comments persistence architecture after separating ordinary reload, local undo, version history, live synchronization, and collaboration?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; Task deep design; Plate Plan and Plite Plan; three bounded Benchmark trials; independent checkpoint, Comments-contract, and history/collaboration attacks
trigger: User accepted the detailed checkpoint-persistence design pass after the final Comments history API audit.
requirements: Keep conversations independent from document undo and preserve exact live-session range mapping through one private native Anchor.
Persist current comment targets with the exact application document revision without serializing anchors on typing.
Keep ordinary reload, persisted local undo, version restore, live sync, and Yjs admission as distinct jobs with one owner each.
Support application-owned authorization and persistence failure through one awaitable mutation boundary.
Pass the frozen one/100/1000/10000 ordinary and Authored range serialization contract before accepting the saved-range target.
Produce a ready implementation and proof plan without implementing unselected product APIs.
evidenceReuse: Reused the current Comments inventory, 29 focused unit/component passes and one Chromium live-undo pass from the preceding review because covered source did not change. Re-read current Comments runtime, persistence and multi-editor consumers, copied UI, Plite Anchor/History/Authored/Yjs boundaries, and history teaching. Reused the original reload and failed serialization receipts, then ran three bounded target trials; the third removed redundant authored resolution and passed every frozen row.
summary: Pursue a smaller architecture and supersede the generic checkpoint requirement. Ordinary Comments reload starts a fresh local undo stack. Live CommentThread records contain semantic data only; a private Anchor owns location, attachment(id) exposes attached or neutral unavailable, and an explicit versioned CommentsJSON exports checkpoint-bound EditorDocumentRange values with the exact app revision. Cut setThreads/live replacement and separate semantic from attachment subscriptions. Add one server-first async mutation adapter. Defer persisted-anchor local History, changed-baseline Yjs target transport, and non-text targets as separate features. The selected authored range optimization passes the frozen 10000-anchor gate by omitting a redundant resolved Range.
alternatives: Generic document/ranges/History/plugin checkpoint: reject for Comments; persisted browser undo is not a current Comments job and the abstraction conflates unrelated lifetimes.
Plain Range persistence: reject as the final target because it drops root, association, deletion policy, and optional Authored identity.
Persist local History by default: reject; ordinary reload and application version history start fresh editor sessions.
Keep a mapped Range in every live thread: reject; it duplicates the native Anchor and turns document mapping into semantic record churn.
Use setThreads for live sync: reject; replacing records from another advanced editor cannot prove target lineage or ordering.
Expose deleted from null/collapsed range: reject; unavailable Authored projections and absent revision targets are observationally identical.
Optimistic comment writes with rollback: reject for v1; server-first publication gives one durable state and preserves composers on failure.
Mandatory activity log, tombstone store, Authored dependency, quote matching, or path-based non-text targets: reject as duplicate or unsound owners.
proofLimits: This is an accepted design and disposable performance receipt, not product implementation. The optimized authored codec is reverted from production source and still needs strict codec tests plus a final production-path benchmark rerun. No CommentsJSON, attachment API, mutation adapter, subscription split, caller migration, browser adoption, or doctrine repair exists yet. The package cannot reject a same-shaped foreign document without the application revision association. Changed-baseline Yjs restore, persisted local undo with anchor recovery, non-text targets, and full Google Docs parity remain explicitly unsupported.
